C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE.IntentSummary: Make the extension trust lifecycle coherent end to end: the incoming data routes (/ext/text-insert, /ext/context, /ext/apply) get the same post-authentication disable fence the /stream/* routes already have — authenticate_incoming snapshots the authorization_epoch beside the resolved id and every data handler re-checks it under stream_gate before any dedup, fence, validation or emit, refusing 401 with the file's plain "extension is not enabled" body and a distinct BLOCK_ log; a disable in flight drains the pending /ext/context reads it owns (the woken handler re-checks the epoch before serving or recording anything, a late renderer response is discarded, nothing enters EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS); a disable whose credential revocation failed records a persistent revoke-pending marker beside the credential so the retry-enable path can no longer silently re-arm the surviving secret — re-arming requires an explicit successful revocation retry or a fresh pairing, mt_ext_enable answers ext_enable_revoke_pending meanwhile, and the gallery's retry keeps sending Disable with the refusal surfaced through a new ten-locale instruction key; and a rebind whose manifest has grown shows every added capability in the pairing dialog before any grant is overwritten (equality and narrowing dialogs state the grant truth instead of today's unconditional "a rebind changes no grant set"), with the dialogs never displaying a caller-reported name that contradicts the registered manifest. Proven by failing-first read_pause fence pins on apply and insert, the context-cancellation pin with its no-binding 409 proof and late-response discard, the revoke-penable enable-refusal family with both clear-on-proof paths and the unreadable-marker refusal, the gallery retry-sync and instruction-mapping vitest pins with the locale parity pin, the pure rebind-classification and name-trust helper pins with harness-approved growth/narrowing/legacy paths, and the unchanged predecessor suites (disable-revocation, grant-bound, rebind, stream-security, binding matrix, incoming refusals) with zero moved pins.

Design decisions locked by this plan: (1) Fence mechanism — authenticate_incoming returns IncomingIdentity { extension_id, authorization_epoch } (the epoch snapshotted via registry.authorization_epoch on the resolved id before return; a disable already landed at resolution keeps today's BLOCK_AUTH_FAILED_INCOMING 401); every data handler takes stream_gate immediately after authentication — before any dedup, binding fence, validation or emit — re-checks IncomingIdentity against the registry exactly like StreamIdentity::is_enabled, refuses 401 with the plain "extension is not enabled" body plus BLOCK_INCOMING_FENCE_REFUSED (route= and id= fields), and holds the gate across the in-memory pre-emit section only (apply: re-check → binding lookup → emit loop; insert: re-check → emit; context: re-check → pending registration, the gate RELEASED before the 5 s wait); no keyring I/O, no bounded renderer wait and no session mutation join the gate; today's lock order (stream_gate, then session, then leaf std Mutexes) is preserved. (2) Composed route order, the invariant regardless of merge order with #321: capability authentication → enabled fence (this change) → #321's dedup short-circuit → binding fence → #321's op validation → emit/ack; anchors are anchor-semantic ("immediately after the authenticate_incoming call in each data handler") and are re-anchored on the merged tree. (3) Context cancellation — the pending value gains the extension id inside live_server.rs (struct PendingContextEntry; the main.rs literal stays textually unchanged); mt_ext_disable drains the disabled extension's entries under stream_gate (pub(super) fn drain_pending_context, BLOCK_DISABLE_CONTEXT_DRAINED count); the woken handler re-checks the epoch under stream_gate before answering or recording — the choice is fixed YES to the pre-serve re-check (review minor a), because it bounds even a response that legitimately overtook the drain: disabled ⇒ 401 fence voice BLOCK_EXT_CONTEXT_CANCELLED with nothing recorded, still-enabled channel closure keeps the existing 500 voice, late responses stay dropped by the unchanged listener. (4) Revoke-pending — the marker is auth.rs's third record (revoke_pending_key "ext:{ext_id}:revoke_pending", a constant value, no secret material, MEM mirror, its own backend family with test injection, store/get/clear with the store_grant discipline at auth.rs:213-232) precisely because re-discovery's state-overwriting register (registry.rs:91-110) cannot touch auth.rs records; the marker is written on the EXISTING ext_disable_revoke_failed branch AFTER the failure is known — marker-before-revoke is rejected because it would mark every successful disable pending too — and a marker write failing alongside the revocation failure (a backend that cannot delete usually cannot write) is the distinct logged BLOCK_DISABLE_REVOKE_PENDING_UNRECORDED residual, documented in the auth.rs MODULE_CONTRACT, not handled (review minor b); mt_ext_enable refuses Err("ext_enable_revoke_pending") before the mint and before stream_gate (BLOCK_ENABLE_REVOKE_PENDING; an unreadable marker BLOCK_ENABLE_REVOKE_PENDING_UNREADABLE — one machine code, two log states); the marker clears on proof only — a successful disable (strict persistent and memory absence; the clear is best-effort with BLOCK_REVOKE_PENDING_CLEAR_FAILED logged, the idempotent retry-disable being the recovery) or a successful pairing (best-effort BLOCK_PAIR_REVOKE_PENDING_CLEARED / _CLEAR_FAILED after the rebind proof, before BLOCK_PAIR_OK). (5) Gallery retry — a per-id revoke-pending set in index.vue; the action is mt_ext_disable when the id is pending or the flag is enabled; pending is added on ext_disable_revoke_failed, removed on a successful disable and whenever the refetched list shows the extension enabled; the ext_enable_revoke_pending refusal surfaces t('extensions.revokePending', ...) — the single new gallery-visible key, shipped under the extensions namespace in all ten locales with non-empty native copy and pinned by FEEDBACK_KEYS (review minor c: the inherited fallback-only extensions.reapprovalRequired gap stays a recorded B3 non-goal and is not repeated here). (6) Rebind honesty — classify_grant_change (pure; Growth{added}/Equal/Narrow over the stored grant vs the declared incoming set; a None stored grant classifies as growth over everything declared) runs before the approval decision; an unreadable stored grant is BLOCK_PAIR_GRANT_UNREADABLE 500 pairing nothing; the growth dialog keeps the key-replacement statement and enumerates every added capability's grant phrase in all() order; equality states no grant change; narrowing names the accesses that stop being served; the capture rule is unchanged (declared∩all() in all() order); the denial branch is byte-unchanged — the harness auto-approves by design, so deny-safety is pinned through the pure descriptions plus the unchanged refusal branch and the unproven-rebind pin keeping the prior grant and key fully valid. (7) Name trust — pairing_display_name (pure, beside pairing_grant_description) yields the registered manifest's name for a registered id, the reported name for an unregistered one, and a distinct mismatch flag; a mismatch is BLOCK_PAIR_NAME_MISMATCH log-only, no refusal (review minor e — the justification is spec Goal 5's: the id anchors authorization, the name is advisory, and refusing would let a lying caller disrupt a legitimate pairing). (8) Apply emit→ack boundary (review minor d) — the fence guarantees emit ordering: every mt::text::op passes the fence first; ops emitted under the gate before a disable lands answer applied:true even when the disable completes before the HTTP ack is written; no un-emit or rollback exists or is attempted; the disable's own fence and doc_close govern everything after; a fenced refusal never answers ok:true or applied:true. (9) Verification — the two MustPassCommands below are the executed forms; the spec's second ExpectedCommand names the extensionGallery/textOps pair: deviation recorded deliberately, textOps.test.js is an untouched regression-only suite (still green, run as task evidence) while locale-keys.test.js is load-bearing because this change adds a locale key. (10) This draft carries no SpecSha256 field; the orchestrator computes and injects it over the approved spec bytes at admission, per the drafting instruction. Deviation note (one, deliberate): the spec enumerates an exact fifteen-file ObservedWriteScope; this plan appends .grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml because the spec's own constraints require the GRACE surface to stay synchronized and task T-007 writes those governed files — the same extension the C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND, C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE and C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND plans applied over their specs.
